chapter: Later career and The Benny Goodman Story
title: The Dallas centennial incident and the police chief
summary: A professor sends champagne backstage, a policeman throws him out, and the Dallas police chief tells Wilson and Hampton he would protect them.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: We had one incident in Dallas, Texas, very interesting. At the centennial down there, about 1937, I guess, and there was some ruckus backstage. A friend of mine, one of the professors from the University of Texas, had a few drinks and then sent some champagne backstage to Lionel and me. And he not only sent it back but after the show he wanted to come back and join us and drink with us. And a security policeman on duty back there said he couldn't drink the champagne with us, he couldn't stay and drink it with us. And he insisted on drinking it with us so this policeman threw him out.

So the next day the police chief called all the policemen at the fair on the carpet and wanted to know what the trouble was. And the situation was explained to him, what happened, and then the Dallas police chief asked for me and Lionel, had us in his office and he told us that he appreciated

what we were doing and most of the people in the South were tired of the old handkerchief-head way of life, and the people appreciated performances like what we were doing in this mixed group. And he said, "And you boys will not have any trouble. If you have the slightest trouble at all, you come and let me know, because I'm the baddest man here." That's the police chief of Dallas, Texas. 1937, in his little speech to Lionel Hampton and me. "If anybody bothers y'all, boys, anybody bothers y'all, boys, just let me know, because I'm the baddest man here."

But that would be the only incident, and that was kind of a side incident, in that this man wanted to -- he had a few drinks and wanted to drink the champagne with us backstage, which was not customary. That was out of the custom. There was no mixed drinking or eating in public places in Texas in those days. And this policeman backstage, he couldn't bring himself to allow it. It was against everything he had been brought up to --
